scenes.recognized_speech: A digit has a value and a position. The digit sum forgets the positions, but a count of written digits must consider every position. Break a range count into the ones, tens and hundreds places, then add those separate counts.

The AMC can ask how often a digit is written, work in complete blocks, then inspect the last incomplete block. In MAWA primary application practice, digit sum restrictions can be combined with range restrictions, use place value to prove which cases count.
What remainder does 386 leave after division by 9? Use its digits to find the remainder without long division. 10 and 100 both leave remainder 1 when divided by 9.
100, 10 and 1 each contribute the same remainder as 1. The digit sum is 3 plus 8 plus 6, which is 17. The remainder of that sum is 8, which is also the remainder of 386.
Write every whole number from 1 through 247. How many times do you write the digit 3? Each occurrence counts separately. Track the ones, tens and hundreds separately.

In the ones place, every complete block of 10 contributes one occurrence, with a possible extra at the end. The ones total is 25. In the tens place, each complete hundred contains one run of 10 occurrences, include any matching part of the last hundred, that gives 30. In the hundreds place, only the block starting at 300 could match. It contributes zero, adding the three totals gives 55 written occurrences.

Write the multiples of 9 from 100 through 599, including any endpoint that is a multiple count every written 3. Split the appearances among the 3 places. A number can contribute in more than one place.

Fix the 1's digit at 3, for each 100's digit, choose a 10's digit, so the 3 digits add to a multiple of 9. Each required remainder for the 10's digit gives 1 choice, except remainder 0 gives 0 and 9. None of the allowed 100's digits gives that double choice. The 10's count is the same, since swapping the 2N digits preserves the digit sum and the 100's range. Each of these places contributes 5.

For the hundreds place, fix the hundreds digit instead. The hundred block starting at 300 contributes 11 occurrences, one for every multiple of 9 in that block. Add the three position counts. An occurrence in one position is different from an occurrence in another, even in the same number. The total is 21.

If a number contains the requested digit twice, it contributes two occurrences, compare counting numbers with counting written digits. Digits 0 and 9 both have remained a 0 on division by 9, include both when 0 is permitted in the position.

Write whether you need a sum, a number of valid integers or a count of written occurrences, record the exact range. Use place value blocks or digit sum restrictions to organize the work. Check an end point and a number with a repeated digit before totalling.
